newsitem.title: USA: Most IMM currency futures settle higher.
newsitem.headline: Most IMM currency futures settle higher.

text.p: Most IMM currency futures settled higher after talk of dollar intervention sparked a midsession rally, forex traders and analysts said.

June yen rallied to $0.007980, from $0.007935, within five minutes due to talk that several Asian and European banks were checking around to possibly sell dollar/yen. June yen's spike filled a chart gap from last Friday's low to Monday's high.

One U.S. dealer reportedly sold $3 billion dollar/yen at 126.80, with one hedge fund selling 1,000 June yen at $0.007935 in the pit, several traders said. The $0.007935 futures level corresponds to the 126.80 spot rate.
While June yen capped gains early in the session, Canadian dollar futures continued to rally into the close, traders said.
Traders and brokers at large U.S. banks said fund buying was heavy in Canadian dollars, even after the Bank of Canada sold Canadian dollars for U.S. dollars at C$1.3870.

"Fund managers have been trying to buy Canadian dollars for the last two months, and have been pretty unsuccessful," one currency broker said, referring to the sideways to downtrend in June Canadian dollars. June set a contract low of $0.7155 on Tuesday.
One floor trader said buy-stop orders were touched off at $0.7200, $0.7216 and into the $0.7230 area.
Another trader expects funds to buy Canadian dollars and sell Australian dollars in the next six months on expectations that the Bank of Canada may raise interest rates.
"Certainly, the Canadian markets are hostage to the U.S. bond markets," another currency trader said.

June sterling closed unchanged ahead of the results of the British elections. Exit polls are expected to be released soon after voting ends at 1600 CDT/2100 GMT, but they said the market has already priced in a Labour party victory.
Some traders are now casting their eyes to the French elections at the end of the month, and noted light French franc selling against the cash marks.
Meanwhile, June marks and Swiss francs were higher, but trade was quiet due to the May Day holidays, they said.

They also said the market was afternoon activity was quiet due to U.S. employment data on Friday. Both the U.S. April unemployment and nonfarm payrolls will be released. Traders are estimating that payrolls will rise to 211,000, from 175,000 in March. The unemployment rate is forecast to stay unchanged at 5.2 percent.
Average hourly earnings are estimated to rise 0.3 percent, from up 0.4 percent.

At the end of pit trade, June yen was up $0.000021 at $0.007946, marks were up $0.0024 at $0.5824, Swiss francs were up $0.0006 at $0.6835, sterling was unchanged at $1.6226, Canadian dollars were up $0.0054 at $0.7233, and Australian dollars were up $0.0036 at $0.7842.
